description: Question bank generated from FDA_SDA_Computer_Knowledge_18_4_Operating_Systems.pdf. Covers OS fundamentals, Windows, shortcuts, Linux, commands, files/folders, extensions, file management, file systems, settings, comparisons and high-yield facts. Verify before formal use.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an operating system (OS)?

options.A: An application for editing documents
options.B: System software that manages hardware and software resources and provides common services and an interface
options.C: A hardware component inside the CPU

questions.explanation: An OS is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services and an interface for users and application programs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main purpose of an operating system?

options.A: To create spreadsheets
options.B: To make a computer usable by managing processor, memory, files, storage, devices, security and application execution

questions.explanation: The main purpose is to make a computer usable by managing its processor, memory, files, storage, devices, security and application execution.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the relationship between user, application software, operating system and hardware?

options.A: User → hardware → OS → application
options.B: User interacts with application software or OS interface; OS manages resources; hardware performs physical operations
options.C: Hardware interacts with user directly without OS
options.D: Application software manages hardware directly without OS

questions.explanation: A user interacts with application software or the OS interface; the OS manages resources and provides services; hardware performs underlying physical operations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a kernel?

options.A: A graphical desktop theme
options.B: The central part of an OS that manages CPU scheduling, memory, device access and system calls

questions.explanation: The kernel is the central part of an OS managing essential functions such as CPU scheduling, memory, device access and system calls.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a shell?

options.A: A hardware casing of the computer
options.B: An interface or command interpreter through which a user or program requests OS services

questions.explanation: A shell is an interface or command interpreter through which a user or program requests OS services; it may be command-line based or graphical.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a desktop environment?

options.A: A collection of graphical components such as panels, menus, windows, icons and file-management tools providing a consistent graphical workspace
options.B: A physical desk where computers are kept

questions.explanation: A desktop environment is a collection of graphical components that provides a consistent graphical workspace.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a user interface (UI)?

options.A: A type of monitor
options.B: The means through which a person interacts with a computer or software

questions.explanation: A UI is the means through which a person interacts with a computer or software, such as graphical interface, command line, touchscreen or voice interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does GUI stand for?

options.A: General User Interface

questions.explanation: GUI stands for Graphical User Interface, allowing interaction through windows, icons, menus, buttons and pointers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does CLI stand for?

options.A: Computer Language Interface

questions.explanation: CLI stands for Command-Line Interface, allowing users to interact by typing text commands.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between GUI and CLI?

options.A: GUI uses typed commands; CLI uses graphics
options.B: GUI uses graphical elements and pointing/touch interaction; CLI uses typed commands

questions.explanation: A GUI uses graphical elements and pointing or touch interaction, while a CLI uses typed commands. CLI is useful for scripting and administration; GUI is easier for visual interaction.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is multitasking?

options.A: Using multiple monitors
options.B: The ability of an OS to manage multiple tasks or programs during the same period by scheduling CPU time and sharing resources

questions.explanation: Multitasking is the ability of an OS to manage multiple tasks or programs during the same period by scheduling CPU time and sharing system resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is multi-user operating-system support?

options.A: Allowing more than one user account to access the same computer system or its services with separate permissions and resources
options.C: Running multiple applications by one user

questions.explanation: Multi-user support allows more than one user account to access the same computer system or its services, with separate permissions and resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is booting?

options.A: Installing an application
options.B: The process of starting or restarting a computer, initialising hardware through firmware and loading the OS

questions.explanation: Booting is the process of starting or restarting a computer, initialising hardware through firmware and loading the operating system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cold boot?

options.A: Restarting without power-off
options.B: Starting a computer from a powered-off state

questions.explanation: A cold boot starts a computer from a powered-off state.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a warm boot?

options.A: Starting from a completely powered-off state
options.B: Restarting a computer without first performing a complete power-off

questions.explanation: A warm boot restarts a computer without first performing a complete power-off, usually through the OS's restart command.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a login?

options.A: Shutting down the computer
options.B: The process by which a user accesses an account by presenting credentials

questions.explanation: A login is the process by which a user accesses an account by presenting credentials such as a password, PIN, security key or biometric factor.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a user account?

options.A: A bank account
options.B: An identity maintained by an OS or service that determines a user's settings, files and access permissions

questions.explanation: A user account is an identity maintained by an OS or service that determines a user's settings, files and access permissions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an administrator account?

options.A: An account with no permissions
options.B: An account with elevated privileges to make system-wide changes, install software, manage users and modify protected settings

questions.explanation: An administrator account has elevated privileges to make system-wide changes, install software, manage users and modify protected settings; such privileges should be used carefully.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a standard user account?

options.A: An account with full administrative control
options.B: An account with limited permissions for everyday work that normally cannot make certain system-wide changes without administrator approval
options.C: An account that cannot log in

questions.explanation: A standard user account has limited permissions for everyday work and normally cannot make certain system-wide changes without administrator approval.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a system update?

options.A: Installing a new hardware component
options.B: Installing changes to an OS such as security fixes, bug corrections, reliability improvements or new features

questions.explanation: A system update installs changes to an operating system, such as security fixes, bug corrections, reliability improvements or new features.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Microsoft Windows?

options.A: An open-source Linux distribution
options.B: A family of proprietary operating systems developed by Microsoft and widely used on personal computers and in organisations

questions.explanation: Microsoft Windows is a family of proprietary operating systems developed by Microsoft and widely used on personal computers and in organisations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Who developed the Windows operating system?

options.A: Apple Corporation

questions.explanation: Microsoft Corporation developed the Windows operating-system family.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Windows desktop?

options.A: The main graphical workspace displayed after a user signs in, commonly containing the taskbar, desktop icons, shortcuts and the Start menu

questions.explanation: The Windows desktop is the main graphical workspace displayed after a user signs in, commonly containing the taskbar, desktop icons, shortcuts and the Start menu.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Start menu in Windows?

options.A: A file compression tool
options.B: An interface providing access to installed applications, search, user-account options, power controls and other system functions

questions.explanation: The Start menu provides access to installed applications, search, user-account options, power controls and other system functions; its design varies across Windows versions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the taskbar in Windows?

options.A: A desktop interface element used to access pinned applications, view running applications, switch between windows and access system-tray controls

questions.explanation: The taskbar is a desktop interface element used to access pinned applications, view running applications, switch between windows and access system-tray or notification-area controls.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the notification area or system tray?

options.A: A folder for notifications
options.B: The part of the Windows taskbar that displays selected status icons and background-application notifications such as network, sound, battery and security status

questions.explanation: The notification area is the part of the Windows taskbar that displays selected status icons and background-application notifications, such as network, sound, battery and security status.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is File Explorer in Windows?

options.A: A web browser
options.B: The Windows file-management application used to browse drives, folders and files and perform operations such as copying, moving, renaming and deleting

questions.explanation: File Explorer is the Windows file-management application used to browse drives, folders and files and perform operations such as copying, moving, renaming and deleting.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Recycle Bin in Windows?

options.A: A special location that temporarily holds many deleted local files so they can be restored or permanently removed

questions.explanation: The Recycle Bin is a special location that temporarily holds many deleted local files so they can be restored or permanently removed. Files deleted from removable media, network locations or with certain commands may bypass it.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which deleted files may bypass the Recycle Bin?

options.A: Files deleted from the Desktop
options.B: Files deleted from removable media, network locations or with certain commands
options.C: All files always go to Recycle Bin

questions.explanation: Files deleted from removable media, network locations or with certain commands may bypass the Recycle Bin.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Control Panel in Windows?

options.A: A traditional Windows interface for viewing and changing various system settings such as devices, programs, user accounts and network options
options.B: A physical control panel on the monitor

questions.explanation: Control Panel is a traditional Windows interface for viewing and changing various system settings. Some settings have moved to the Settings app in newer Windows versions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Settings app in Windows?

options.A: The modern Windows interface for configuring system options such as display, sound, network, Bluetooth, accounts, privacy, updates and accessibility

questions.explanation: The Settings app is the modern Windows interface for configuring system options such as display, sound, network, Bluetooth, accounts, privacy, updates and accessibility.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between Control Panel and Settings in Windows?

options.A: They are identical
options.B: Settings is the modern configuration interface with many current options; Control Panel is the older interface that remains available for some settings and administrative tasks
options.C: Control Panel is newer than Settings
options.D: Settings is only for network configuration

questions.explanation: Settings is the modern configuration interface and contains many current system options; Control Panel is the older configuration interface that remains available for some settings and administrative tasks. The exact division depends on the Windows version.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Windows search feature?

options.A: A tool to search the internet only
options.B: A feature that helps users find applications, settings, files and other content by entering search terms in the Start menu or search interface

questions.explanation: Windows Search helps users find applications, settings, files and other content by entering search terms in the Start menu or search interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Windows Task Manager?

options.A: A utility to view and manage running applications, processes, CPU and memory usage, startup applications, users and performance information

questions.explanation: Task Manager is a Windows utility used to view and manage running applications, processes, CPU and memory usage, startup applications, users and selected performance information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which shortcut opens Task Manager directly in Windows?

options.A: Ctrl + Shift + Esc

questions.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager directly.
questions.source: Section B, Section C and Section M

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Windows Update?

options.A: A service for delivering supported Windows updates including security patches, quality improvements and feature updates
options.B: A tool for updating hardware drivers only

questions.explanation: Windows Update is Microsoft's service and feature for delivering supported Windows updates, including security patches, quality improvements and feature updates.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Microsoft Defender Antivirus?

options.A: A web browser
options.B: Microsoft's built-in anti-malware protection component in supported Windows versions that helps detect, block and remove malicious software

questions.explanation: Microsoft Defender Antivirus is Microsoft's built-in anti-malware protection component in supported Windows versions. It helps detect, block and remove malicious software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Windows Security?

options.A: A web browser security setting
options.B: The Windows application that provides access to security features and status information including virus and threat protection, firewall, account protection and device security

questions.explanation: Windows Security is the Windows application that provides access to security features and status information, including virus and threat protection, firewall and network protection, account protection and device security.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Device Manager in Windows?

options.A: A tool to manage user accounts
options.B: An administrative tool that displays installed hardware devices and their drivers and allows users to inspect device status, update or roll back drivers and troubleshoot hardware issues

questions.explanation: Device Manager is a Windows administrative tool that displays installed hardware devices and their drivers and allows users to inspect device status, update or roll back drivers, disable devices and troubleshoot certain hardware issues.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Disk Management in Windows?

options.A: A utility used to view and manage disks and partitions, including creating, formatting, deleting and resizing supported volumes

questions.explanation: Disk Management is a Windows utility used to view and manage disks and partitions, including creating, formatting, deleting and resizing supported volumes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Windows Command Prompt?

options.A: A command-line application in Windows that runs commands through the command interpreter, commonly cmd.exe

questions.explanation: Command Prompt is a command-line application in Windows that runs commands through the command interpreter, commonly cmd.exe.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Windows PowerShell?

options.A: A web browser
options.B: A command-line shell and scripting language designed for task automation and system administration, working with cmdlets

questions.explanation: PowerShell is a command-line shell and scripting language designed for task automation and system administration. It works with commands called cmdlets and can also run scripts.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between Command Prompt and PowerShell?

options.A: They are identical
options.B: Command Prompt is the traditional Windows command interpreter; PowerShell is a more powerful shell and scripting environment with structured objects, cmdlets and automation features
options.C: PowerShell is older than Command Prompt
options.D: Command Prompt is only for Linux

questions.explanation: Command Prompt is the traditional Windows command interpreter, while PowerShell is a more powerful shell and scripting environment with structured objects, cmdlets and extensive automation features.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Windows shortcut?

options.A: A link or reference to a file, folder, application or location; deleting it normally does not delete the original item

questions.explanation: A shortcut is a link or reference to a file, folder, application or location. Deleting a shortcut normally does not delete the original item it points to.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is sleep mode in Windows?

options.A: A mode that places the computer in a low-power state while keeping the session in memory so it can resume quickly
options.B: A mode that saves the session to storage and powers down fully
options.C: A mode that shuts down the computer completely
options.D: A mode that restarts the computer

questions.explanation: Sleep mode places a computer in a low-power state while keeping the session in memory so it can resume quickly. Some devices use modern standby rather than traditional sleep.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is hibernation in Windows?

options.A: A mode that keeps the session in memory only
options.B: A mode that saves the current session state to non-volatile storage and powers the computer down, allowing the session to be restored later
options.C: A mode that restarts the computer
options.D: A mode that locks the screen

questions.explanation: Hibernation saves the current session state to non-volatile storage and powers the computer down, allowing the session to be restored later while using very little or no operating power.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between Sleep and Hibernate?

options.A: Sleep keeps the session in memory and uses a small amount of power for quick resume; Hibernate saves the session to storage and powers down more fully
options.B: Sleep saves to storage; Hibernate keeps in memory

questions.explanation: Sleep keeps the session in memory and uses a small amount of power for quick resume; Hibernate saves the session to storage and powers down more fully, usually taking longer to resume.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What happens during sign-out in Windows?

options.A: It closes the current user's session and applications but does not necessarily shut down the computer; another user can then sign in
options.B: It powers off the computer completely

questions.explanation: Sign-out closes the current user's session and applications but does not necessarily shut down the computer. Another user can then sign in.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between Restart and Shut down in Windows?

options.A: Restart closes the current session and starts Windows again; Shut down powers off the computer
options.B: Restart powers off the computer; Shut down restarts it

questions.explanation: Restart closes the current session and starts Windows again; Shut down powers off the computer. Some Windows configurations use Fast Startup, so a normal shutdown may not be identical to a full restart.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why may a normal shutdown not be identical to a full restart in some Windows configurations?

options.A: Because of Fast Startup

questions.explanation: Some Windows configurations use Fast Startup, so a normal shutdown may not be identical to a full restart.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Windows clipboard?

options.A: A temporary storage area used to hold copied or cut content so it can be pasted elsewhere

questions.explanation: The clipboard is a temporary storage area used to hold copied or cut content, such as text, images and files, so it can be pasted elsewhere.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Windows Snipping Tool?

options.A: A utility used to capture screenshots or selected portions of the screen

questions.explanation: Snipping Tool is a Windows utility used to capture screenshots or selected portions of the screen, with features varying by Windows version.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Windows Task View?

options.A: A feature that provides an overview of open windows and virtual desktops, allowing users to switch between tasks and organise workspaces

questions.explanation: Task View provides an overview of open windows and virtual desktops, allowing users to switch between tasks and organise workspaces.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a virtual desktop in Windows?

options.A: A separate workspace that can contain its own arrangement of open application windows, helping users organise tasks without another physical monitor

questions.explanation: A virtual desktop is a separate workspace that can contain its own arrangement of open application windows, helping users organise tasks without requiring another physical monitor.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + C do in Windows?

options.A: Copies the selected text, file or other supported item to the clipboard

questions.explanation: Ctrl + C copies the selected text, file or other supported item to the clipboard.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + X do in Windows?

options.A: Copies the selected item
options.B: Cuts the selected text or item, placing it on the clipboard so it can be moved when pasted

questions.explanation: Ctrl + X cuts the selected text or item, placing it on the clipboard so it can be moved when pasted.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + V do in Windows?

options.A: Copies the selected item
options.C: Pastes the current clipboard contents at the selected location

questions.explanation: Ctrl + V pastes the current clipboard contents at the selected location.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + Z do in Windows?

options.A: Redoes an action
options.B: Generally undoes the most recent supported action in the active application

questions.explanation: Ctrl + Z generally undoes the most recent supported action in the active application.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + Y do in Windows?

options.A: Undoes an action
options.B: Commonly redoes or repeats an action that was undone, depending on the application

questions.explanation: Ctrl + Y commonly redoes or repeats an action that was undone, depending on the application.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + A do in Windows?

options.A: Opens a new window
options.B: Selects all items or all text in the active context, where supported

questions.explanation: Ctrl + A selects all items or all text in the active context, where supported.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + S do in most Windows applications?

options.A: Saves the current document or file

questions.explanation: Ctrl + S saves the current document or file in most applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + P do in most Windows applications?

options.A: Saves the document

questions.explanation: Ctrl + P opens the print interface in most applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Alt + Tab do in Windows?

options.A: Closes the active window

questions.explanation: Alt + Tab switches between open application windows.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Alt + F4 do in Windows?

options.A: Opens File Explorer
options.B: Closes the active window or application; if no application window is active, it may open the Windows shutdown interface

questions.explanation: Alt + F4 closes the active window or application; if no application window is active, it may open the Windows shutdown interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Windows key + D do?

options.A: Shows or hides the desktop by minimising or restoring windows

questions.explanation: Windows key + D shows or hides the desktop by minimising or restoring windows.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Windows key + E do?

options.A: Opens Settings

questions.explanation: Windows key + E opens File Explorer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Windows key + L do?

options.A: Locks the computer or current Windows session

questions.explanation: Windows key + L locks the computer or current Windows session.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Windows key + I do?

options.A: Opens File Explorer
options.B: Opens the Windows Settings app in supported Windows versions

questions.explanation: Windows key + I opens the Windows Settings app in supported Windows versions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Windows key + R do?

options.A: Opens the Run dialog box

questions.explanation: Windows key + R opens the Run dialog box.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Windows key + S do?

options.A: Saves the document
options.B: Opens the Windows search interface in supported versions

questions.explanation: Windows key + S opens the Windows search interface in supported versions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Windows key + Tab do?

options.A: Opens Task View, showing open windows and virtual desktops

questions.explanation: Windows key + Tab opens Task View, showing open windows and virtual desktops.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + Shift + Esc do?

options.A: Opens Task Manager directly

questions.explanation: Ctrl + Shift + Esc opens Task Manager directly.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Ctrl + Alt + Delete do in Windows?

options.A: Restarts the computer immediately
options.B: Opens the Windows security screen, from which users can access options such as lock, switch user, sign out, Task Manager and security-related actions

questions.explanation: Ctrl + Alt + Delete opens the Windows security screen, from which users can access options such as lock, switch user, sign out, Task Manager and security-related actions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does F2 do in Windows File Explorer?

options.A: Refreshes the view
options.B: Renames the selected file or folder

questions.explanation: F2 renames the selected file or folder.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does F5 do in many Windows interfaces?

options.A: Renames the selected file
options.B: Refreshes or reloads the current view in many applications, including File Explorer and web browsers

questions.explanation: F5 refreshes or reloads the current view in many applications, including File Explorer and web browsers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does the Delete key do to a selected file in File Explorer?

options.A: Permanently deletes the file
options.B: Normally moves a selected local file or folder to the Recycle Bin, subject to location and system settings

questions.explanation: Delete normally moves a selected local file or folder to the Recycle Bin, subject to location and system settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Shift + Delete do to a selected file in Windows?

options.A: Moves the file to the Recycle Bin
options.B: Normally deletes the selected item without moving it to the Recycle Bin; recovery may still be possible but it should be treated as a permanent-delete action

questions.explanation: Shift + Delete normally deletes the selected item without moving it to the Recycle Bin. Recovery may still be possible in some circumstances, but it should be treated as a permanent-delete action.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Windows key + Shift + S do?

options.A: Opens the screen-snipping interface in supported Windows versions, allowing the user to capture a selected screen area

questions.explanation: Windows key + Shift + S opens the screen-snipping interface in supported Windows versions, allowing the user to capture a selected screen area.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is Linux?

options.A: An open-source, Unix-like operating-system kernel; a complete Linux OS is commonly provided as a distribution
options.B: A proprietary operating system developed by Microsoft

questions.explanation: Linux is an open-source, Unix-like operating-system kernel. A complete Linux operating system is commonly provided as a distribution that combines the kernel with system utilities, libraries and applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Who created the Linux kernel and in which year was its first version released?

options.A: Bill Gates, 1985

questions.explanation: Linus Torvalds created the Linux kernel and released its first version in 1991.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is Linux an operating system or a kernel?

options.A: Strictly, Linux is the kernel; in everyday usage it often refers to a complete OS built around that kernel
options.B: Linux is strictly a complete operating system, not a kernel

questions.explanation: Strictly, Linux is the kernel. In everyday usage, Linux often refers to a complete operating system built around that kernel, such as Ubuntu or Fedora.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Linux distribution?

options.A: A complete operating-system package that includes the Linux kernel, system utilities, libraries, package-management tools and applications

questions.explanation: A Linux distribution is a complete operating-system package that includes the Linux kernel, system utilities, libraries, package-management tools and applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is a popular Linux distribution?

options.A: Ubuntu

questions.explanation: Popular Linux distributions include Ubuntu, Debian, Fedora, Linux Mint, Arch Linux, openSUSE and Red Hat Enterprise Linux.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Linux terminal?

options.A: A text-based interface through which a user interacts with a shell and enters commands to manage files, run programs and administer the system

questions.explanation: The Linux terminal is a text-based interface through which a user interacts with a shell and enters commands to manage files, run programs and administer the system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a shell in Linux?

options.A: A command interpreter that accepts commands and scripts and requests services from the OS; common shells include Bash, Zsh and Fish

questions.explanation: A Linux shell is a command interpreter that accepts commands and scripts and requests services from the operating system. Common shells include Bash, Zsh and Fish.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does Bash stand for?

options.A: Basic Shell

questions.explanation: Bash stands for Bourne Again Shell. It is a widely used Unix/Linux command-line shell and scripting language.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Linux root user?

options.A: A standard user account
options.B: The superuser account with extensive administrative privileges over the Linux system

questions.explanation: The root user is the superuser account with extensive administrative privileges over the Linux system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the root directory in Linux?

options.A: The home directory of the root user
options.B: The top-level directory of the Linux file-system hierarchy, represented by a forward slash (/)

questions.explanation: The root directory is the top-level directory of the Linux file-system hierarchy and is represented by a forward slash (/). It is not the same as the root user's home directory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which symbol represents the root directory in Linux?

options.A: Backslash (\)

questions.explanation: A forward slash (/) represents the root directory in Linux.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a home directory in Linux?

options.A: The personal directory assigned to a user, commonly located under /home such as /home/alex; the root user's home directory is commonly /root

questions.explanation: A home directory is the personal directory assigned to a user, commonly located under /home, such as /home/alex. The root user's home directory is commonly /root.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of the /home directory in Linux?

options.A: It commonly contains the personal directories and files of ordinary users
options.C: It contains essential user command binaries

questions.explanation: The /home directory commonly contains the personal directories and files of ordinary users.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of the /etc directory in Linux?

options.A: It contains personal user files
options.B: It commonly contains system-wide configuration files

questions.explanation: The /etc directory commonly contains system-wide configuration files.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of the /bin directory in Linux?

options.A: It traditionally contains essential user command binaries; on many modern distributions /bin may be a symbolic link to /usr/bin

questions.explanation: The /bin directory traditionally contains essential user command binaries. On many modern distributions, /bin may be a symbolic link to /usr/bin.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the purpose of the /usr directory in Linux?

options.A: It is the personal home directory of users

questions.question: What is System Restore in Windows?

options.A: A recovery feature that can revert certain system files, registry settings, drivers and installed programs to an earlier restore point without being designed as a personal-file backup
options.B: A feature that backs up personal files only
options.C: A feature that formats the drive
options.D: A feature that installs new applications

questions.explanation: System Restore is a Windows recovery feature that can revert certain system files, registry settings, drivers and installed programs to an earlier restore point without being designed as a personal-file backup.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a factory reset?

options.A: A process that restores a device or OS to a default or near-original software state; depending on the option selected, personal files, applications and settings may be removed
options.B: A process that only restores system files
options.C: A process that backs up personal files
options.D: A process that installs new applications

questions.explanation: A factory reset restores a device or operating system to a default or near-original software state. Depending on the option selected, personal files, applications and settings may be removed.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between a system restore and a factory reset?

options.A: System Restore reverts selected system configuration to an earlier restore point; a factory reset reinstalls or resets the system to a default state and may remove applications, settings and personal data
options.C: System Restore removes all personal files; factory reset keeps them
options.D: Factory reset only restores system files

questions.explanation: System Restore reverts selected system configuration to an earlier restore point; a factory reset reinstalls or resets the system to a default state and may remove applications, settings and personal data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why should system settings be changed carefully?

options.A: Incorrect settings can affect connectivity, security, performance, accessibility or system stability; users should understand the effect of a change and keep backups before making high-impact changes
options.C: System settings are only for display
options.D: System settings never affect the system

questions.explanation: Incorrect settings can affect connectivity, security, performance, accessibility or system stability. Users should understand the effect of a change and keep backups before making high-impact changes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is a restore point a replacement for a backup?

options.A: Yes, it replaces all backups
options.B: No, a restore point is not a replacement for a backup; keep independent copies of important personal files

questions.explanation: A restore point is not a replacement for a backup. Keep independent copies of important personal files.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the main difference between Windows and Linux?

options.A: Windows is a proprietary OS family developed by Microsoft; Linux refers strictly to an open-source kernel and commonly to distributions built around it; their interfaces, licensing, administration tools and software ecosystems differ
options.B: Windows is open source; Linux is proprietary

questions.explanation: Windows is a proprietary operating-system family developed by Microsoft; Linux refers strictly to an open-source kernel and commonly to distributions built around it. Their interfaces, licensing, administration tools and software ecosystems differ.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is Windows open source?

options.A: Yes, Windows is fully open source
options.B: No, the main Windows operating-system code is proprietary and is not distributed as an open-source operating system
options.C: Only older versions are open source
options.D: Only Windows Server is open source

questions.explanation: The main Windows operating-system code is proprietary and is not distributed as an open-source operating system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is Linux free and open source?

options.A: The Linux kernel is open source and many Linux distributions can be downloaded and used without a licence purchase, although commercial support, services and some bundled software may cost money
options.C: Linux always requires a paid licence

questions.explanation: The Linux kernel is open source and many Linux distributions can be downloaded and used without a licence purchase, although commercial support, services and some bundled software may cost money.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Does Windows use drive letters?

options.A: No, Windows never uses drive letters
options.B: Yes, Windows commonly identifies volumes using drive letters such as C: and D:, although it also supports mounted folders and other storage arrangements
options.C: Only older Windows versions use drive letters
options.D: Only removable drives use drive letters

questions.explanation: Windows commonly identifies volumes using drive letters such as C: and D:, although it also supports mounted folders and other storage arrangements.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: How does Linux identify storage locations?

options.A: Linux uses drive letters such as C: and D:
options.B: Linux normally exposes mounted storage within a single directory tree beginning at the root directory (/), rather than relying on drive letters

questions.explanation: Linux normally exposes mounted storage within a single directory tree beginning at the root directory (/), rather than relying on drive letters.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which operating system commonly uses the NTFS file system?

options.A: Linux
options.B: Modern Windows installations commonly use NTFS for their main system volumes

questions.explanation: Modern Windows installations commonly use NTFS for their main system volumes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which file system is commonly used by many Linux distributions?

options.B: ext4, although other file systems such as Btrfs and XFS are also used

questions.explanation: Many Linux distributions commonly use ext4, although other file systems such as Btrfs and XFS are also used.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Is a shortcut the same as the original file?

options.A: Yes, a shortcut is a copy of the original file
options.B: No, a shortcut is a link or reference to the original file or location
options.C: Yes, deleting the shortcut deletes the original file
options.D: Yes, a shortcut contains all the original file's data

questions.explanation: A shortcut is a link or reference to the original file or location, not the original file itself.
